provenance: Captured Tue 1 Sep 2026 from Apple clang on macOS 15 (arm64), built from two trivial C sources: 'int main(void){return 0;}' and 'int mdt_probe(void){return 7;}'. Real linker output, not constructed bytes: each file is a loadable Mach-O that otool -L reads and codesign would accept.
deployment_target: Built with -mmacosx-version-min=11.0 so LC_BUILD_VERSION minos matches the app's own bundle.macOS.minimumSystemVersion in apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json. The first capture defaulted to the host SDK (minos 26.0) and could not have been loaded by the macos-14 packaging runner, which contradicted the loadability claim these fixtures are here to support. A test asserts minos <= that declared minimum, so the two cannot drift apart again.
file_b_note: The file_b string per entry is what macOS file(1) printed when these were captured. It is PROVENANCE, not an assertion target: GNU file words the same binary differently (ubuntu-latest prints 'Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable, flags:<...>'), and it describes a bundle with a phrase containing the one it uses for a shared library. Filetype is read from otool -hv, which prints a token; tests assert only that file(1) says 'Mach-O' at all.

shapes.opendj-probe-executable: MH_EXECUTE with no extension -- runtime/bin/python3.N, the interpreter an extension-only predicate misses
shapes.opendj-probe-bundle.so: MH_BUNDLE named .so -- a CPython extension module
shapes.opendj-probe-dylib-named.so: MH_DYLIB named .so -- the real shape of pydantic_core, rpds, watchfiles, rbox and protobuf's _message.abi3.so, where suffix and filetype disagree

immutable: Canonical fixture. Verify by checksum before use; tests hydrate a disposable copy and never mutate these.

libopendj-probe.dylib.file_b: Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library arm64

opendj-probe-dylib-named.so.file_b: Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library arm64
